scope: Selected verified reports. Strategy overlap is not identical trials or measured wasted compute. Times are relative to each worker session; dots do not show duration. Both final runs FAIL.

events.label: Builds a top-edge grasp
events.quote: I’ve inspected the initial scene visually. I’m building a two-hand grasp around the monitor’s upper edge, with the fingers clear at initialization and joint actuation providing the closing force. The first test will check whether that grasp can hold the object under gravity.

events.label: Stable hold
events.quote: The revised grasp held the monitor for three seconds without a fall or drop. Mean position deviation during the hold was about 1.9 cm. I’m now testing the complete object curve with live arm IK and SONIC controlling the body.

events.label: Stable hold
events.quote: The upper-edge grasp held the monitor for the three-second stationary test with about 2.3 cm position RMSE. During the full curve, it lost contact near the first large rotation, and the robot’s travel diverged from the reference. I’m separating those problems: first testing the rotation with a slower arm motion, then adjusting the locomotion reference.

events.label: Stable hold
events.quote: The top-edge grasp held the monitor for the two-second test, with about 4.1 cm pose-position RMSE against the stationary reference and no drop. I’m now extending it to the full curve, using SONIC for balance and locomotion and joint impedance control for the arms and fingers.

events.label: Stable hold
events.quote: Finger closure substantially improved the hold test: the monitor remained off the floor for the three-second trial, with 3.3 cm object-position RMSE, while the robot stayed upright. I’m extending this to a slower full-curve motion with turning and stepping, followed by lowering the monitor onto the floor.

events.label: Reports side-grasp slip
events.quote: The longer tests exposed two problems: the side grasp eventually slips, and the first walking reference drove the legs into poor configurations. I’ve corrected the leg reference and am testing a top-edge grasp, where the thumb and fingers can contact opposite faces of the monitor.

events.label: Transfer fails
events.quote: The latest walking trial still fell during weight transfer. One final test is running with a much slower transfer and revised arm IK. I’m also testing a conservative controller that pauses reference progress when grip tracking or arm reachability exceeds a margin. If the full curve remains unsuccessful, I’ll mark the submission as incomplete.

events.label: Transfer fails
events.quote: The walking trials still fail during support transfer, despite the stable stationary grasp. I haven’t achieved the complete curve. With the remaining time, I’m testing a controlled set-down so the final submission can avoid a fall or uncontrolled drop. I’ll score it against the entire target and document the incomplete transport clearly.

events.label: Transfer fails
events.quote: Full-curve trials are still failing during weight transfer. I’ve added reference foot velocity and acceleration to the balance controller; the earlier version was lagging the swing-foot motion. The stationary grasp is reliable so far, but I have not yet achieved a complete, fall-free carry.

events.label: Transport incomplete
events.quote: I’ll save the best tested full-reference attempt and stop further trials. It kept the robot upright, but the object dropped and the complete curve was not achieved. I’ll make those limitations explicit in the results.
